t: This is Lambeth Palace, the official London home of the Archbishop of Canterbury. It stands on the south bank of the Thames, almost directly across the river from the Houses of Parliament. Many archbishops have lived and died within these walls. Gilbert Sheldon died here in 1677, and Matthew Parker, who became archbishop in 1559, died here and is buried here too. Charles Manners-Sutton died here in 1828, and Cosmo Lang lived here through the abdication crisis of 1936. More recently, Justin Welby lived here as archbishop from 2013 to 2025.
